extractedItems.title: Testing the Green
extractedItems.question: You are about to putt. Can you test the green by rolling a ball or making the surface rough with your hand?

choices.text: Yes, you can do either
No, both actions are not allowed
Only rolling a ball is allowed
Only roughening the surface is allowed

extractedItems.explanation: Testing the green by rolling a ball or roughening the surface is not allowed and costs 2 penalty strokes.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl on a putting green, kneeling next to her golf ball, with her hand close to the green as if about to touch or roughen it, looking unsure.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl near golf ball on the green, hand close to surface, appearing unsure if she can touch it.

extractedItems.title: Repairing Damage on the Green
extractedItems.question: Which of these types of damage are you allowed to repair on the green without any penalty?

choices.text: Pitch-marks and spike marks
Aeration holes
Old hole plugs
Natural imperfections

extractedItems.explanation: You can repair things like pitch-marks, spike marks, and old hole plugs, but not aeration holes or natural imperfections.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy using a pitch mark repair tool on the putting green where his ball has landed.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy repairing a pitch mark next to his golf ball on the green.

extractedItems.title: What To Do With An Embedded Ball
extractedItems.question: Your ball has become embedded in the putting green after a shot. What should you do?

choices.text: Leave it where it is and play it as it lies
Mark its position, pick it up, repair the pitch-mark, and put the ball back
Pick it up and drop it two club lengths away
Ask another player to move it

extractedItems.explanation: You should mark the spot, lift the ball, repair the pitch-mark, and replace the ball without penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl marking the spot of her embedded golf ball on the green, preparing to pick it up.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl marking position of embedded golf ball on the green.

extractedItems.title: Removing Loose Impediments
extractedItems.question: You're on the green and your ball is next to some leaves, a twig, and a bit of sand. Which can you remove without penalty?

choices.text: Leaves
Twig
Sand
All of them

extractedItems.explanation: On the putting green, you may remove leaves, twigs, and even sand or loose soil without penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy carefully picking up a twig and leaves beside his ball on the putting green.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy removing natural debris from around his golf ball on the green.

extractedItems.title: Dealing with Movable Obstructions
extractedItems.question: You find a lost glove and a scorecard near your ball on the green. What should you do?

choices.text: Play your ball as it lies, without moving anything
Move the glove and scorecard and play your shot
Call for a penalty before touching them
Ask your friend to move them for you

extractedItems.explanation: You can remove movable obstructions like gloves and scorecards without penalty. If your ball moves, just put it back.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl gently picking up a glove and a scorecard next to her golf ball on the putting green.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl lifting a glove and scorecard away from a golf ball on the green.
